title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly Executive Team meeting: first actions after the September board - damp breach deep-dive, Orchard Fields lettings and defects, electrician recruitment, a new Housing Ombudsman evidence request, Copilot pilot conditions and the Q2 board paper timetable.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Silvering Homes Executive Team (Mondays 09:30-10:30, Teams). Action log kept by Tessa Morgan.

transcript.text: Morning, everyone. Can you all hear me? Martin, you're frozen... no, you're back. Right. Tessa, are we recording?
Yes, recording and transcribing. Just to say for the record, this is being transcribed for the action log.
Thanks. So this is our first proper week after the board, and I want to go through the board actions first because Hilary will be watching every one of them. Joanne, can you take us through?

Sure. Six actions from the twenty-fourth. The big one is BA thirty-one - Gareth's deep-dive on Awaab's Law breaches to Hilary by the thirty-first of October. Then thirty-two, CEC to look at A06, which is Thursday. Thirty-three, fire doors and lifts for November. Thirty-four, Orchard Fields void loss in the November development report. Thirty-five, Catherine confirming the Copilot conditions. And thirty-six is mine, the Q2 performance report.
Gareth, the deep-dive. Where are we?
Er, so, I've asked Ellie and Kwame to pull every Awaab's case since last October out of FieldLoop. What I want to do is get you a draft by the twenty-third so you can see it before it goes to Hilary.
Draft to me by the twenty-third. Good. And please, it needs to say who the households were - vulnerability, children - not just a count.
That's the tricky bit, because the vulnerability flag lives in Keystone, not FieldLoop. We'll have to match them by hand.
And just a reminder, if you're doing that matching in Excel, keep it in the Damp & Mould library, not on anyone's desktop. It's exactly the kind of data I'm nervous about.
Yep, understood.
Orchard Fields. Martin, Tom's not here, so it's you.

So we took the homes on the second. First keys went out last Tuesday - Mark Thomas, Flat 1. We're letting steadily, but Castlemere's defects list is over a hundred and forty items and there are heat pump commissioning faults in eleven homes. Paul's view is we'll have a block of homes we can't let until those are cleared.
How many?
Probably around twenty. I'll know better next week. I've asked Paul to get a dated defects programme out of Castlemere by Friday, and Chloe to give me a lettings plan for whatever's left.
Can I just ask that we don't let anyone into a home with a heat pump that isn't working? October's going to turn cold.
Absolutely not. The board was very clear on that.
Repairs. Gareth, the numbers.

September routine in target was about fifty-one per cent. Still bad. Emergencies are fine, ninety-seven, ninety-eight. The issue is the same - two sparks and a plasterer short, and Brightline are... variable.

On recruitment, we've got sign-off for the higher market supplement, so the adverts for both electrician posts and the plasterer go live on Friday the sixteenth. Lauren's also talking to the college about two more apprentices for next September.
Friday. Great. Rachel - complaints.

Two things. September stage 1 was poor - about forty per cent in time - and I know Marcia will raise it on Thursday because of A06. Owen's analysis says almost all the late ones were waiting for information from repairs.
That's fair, to be honest. Planners are stretched.

The second thing is the Ombudsman. We had a letter on Friday on the Brenchley Gardens damp case - Dawn Collins, CMP-24019. They want a full evidence pack by the thirtieth of October. Job history, the surveyor's reports, all the letters we sent her.
That's the one from January last year? That's been going on far too long.
It has. I'll collate it, but I'll need Gareth's team for the repairs history.
Sure, just tell me who and when.
Simone, Copilot.

So on track for the nineteenth. Craig's finished the permissions sweep, the Highly Confidential libraries are excluded and tested, and the policy was signed off at Exec last week. I'll send you the three conditions in writing by Thursday so you can confirm to Hilary.
Thursday's fine. Joanne, Q2 paper.
I'll send round the timetable by Friday. Papers for the twenty-sixth of November due on the twelfth, ten working days. Can I please beg everyone to use the new cover template this time?
Is that the one with the residents' voice box?
That's the one. Version three, on the Hub.
Anything else? No? Okay. Tessa, can you read the actions back?

Gareth, deep-dive draft to Catherine by the twenty-third. Martin, Castlemere defects programme and lettings plan by the nineteenth. Simone, adverts live on the sixteenth, and Copilot conditions to Catherine by the fifteenth. Rachel, Ombudsman evidence pack, due the thirtieth, with Gareth's team supporting. Joanne, Q2 timetable by the sixteenth.
Perfect. Thanks all. Same time next week.

recap.summary: First Executive Team meeting after the 24 September board. Gareth Price will give the Chief Executive a draft Awaab's Law breach deep-dive by 23 October, ahead of the 31 October deadline to the Chair. Orchard Fields lettings began on 6 October but more than 140 defects, including heat pump faults in 11 homes, mean around 20 homes may be held back. Electrician and plasterer adverts go live on 16 October with a higher market supplement. The Housing Ombudsman has asked for an evidence pack on the Brenchley Gardens damp case CMP-24019 by 30 October. The Copilot pilot is on track for 19 October.

title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly Executive Team meeting: Copilot pilot goes live, the Customer Experience Committee reopens RSH action A06, 18 Orchard Fields homes held on defects, adverts live and the damp deep-dive draft still due on 23 October.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Silvering Homes Executive Team (Mondays 09:30-10:30, Teams). Action log kept by Tessa Morgan.

transcript.text: Morning. Simone, before anything else - congratulations, Copilot's live.
Thank you! All thirty licences assigned at eight o'clock. Craig had three calls before half past, all 'where's the button', so... that's fine.
I've already had it summarise the management accounts. It got one number wrong, which I found reassuring, in a way.
Which is exactly the message - Copilot drafts, you check.
Tessa, action log please.

Simone, adverts - done, live Friday. Copilot conditions - done, you sent them Thursday. Joanne, Q2 timetable - done, went out Friday. Martin, Castlemere programme and lettings plan - due today. Gareth, deep-dive draft - due Friday. Rachel, Ombudsman pack - due the thirtieth.
Martin?

Partly. Chloe's lettings plan is done. Castlemere haven't given us a dated programme, because their site manager left on Wednesday, would you believe. Paul's chasing their contracts director. Where we've landed is forty-four homes let and eighteen we're holding.
Eighteen. And what's that costing us a week?

Around {{sql:SELECT ROUND(SUM(weekly_rent), 0) FROM properties WHERE status = 'New build - awaiting let'|gbp}} a week in rent. Not catastrophic but it adds up, and it'll go in the development report for the board.
Okay. I want the dated programme by next Monday, please. Tell Castlemere I'll ring their MD if needed.
I'll pass that on. Happily.
Rachel, CEC on Thursday.
So, as expected, Marcia went straight to A06. The committee agreed to reopen it, revised date end of March, and the measure is three consecutive months at a hundred per cent. Which is fair.
I'll update the tracker.
Thanks. The other thing - TSMs year to date are better, overall's up to {{fact:tsm_overall_2627_ytd}}, but complaint handling is still terrible. About forty per cent.
Which is the thing the regulator will look at.
Yes. And Owen's fix is really about repairs giving us the information faster.
I've spoken to Kwame. From this week, a planner picks up complaint information requests within two working days, and it's tracked in FieldLoop.
That would make a real difference.
Gareth, while you've got the mic - deep-dive. Friday?
Friday's... going to be tight. Kwame's got the FieldLoop data. The Keystone matching for vulnerability isn't done. But yes, I'll get you something Friday.
Something isn't a draft, Gareth.
No, fair. A draft.
Can I come in on recruitment? Adverts are live. Six enquiries over the weekend, mostly for the plasterer. Closing date the twenty-sixth, interviews the week of the second.
Good. Rachel, Ombudsman pack?
Letters and complaint file are done. I'm waiting for the job history and Ellie's surveyor reports. Gareth, by Tuesday next week, please.
Tuesday. Yep.
One small AOB. The strategy day at Linton Lodge on the twenty-sixth - Hilary wants the Home First refresh pre-read to include what we've learned from the C2. Catherine, are you okay to own that?
Yes, I'll do it. Okay, I think that's us. Thanks everyone.

recap.summary: The Copilot pilot went live on 19 October with all 30 licences assigned. The Customer Experience Committee reopened RSH action A06, with a revised date of 31 March 2027 and a measure of three consecutive months at 100% of stage 1 replies on time. Orchard Fields: 44 homes let and 18 held on defects, at a rent loss of about {{sql:SELECT ROUND(SUM(weekly_rent), 0) FROM properties WHERE status = 'New build - awaiting let'|gbp}} a week. Castlemere has still not provided a dated defects programme because its site manager left. The damp deep-dive draft is still due on Friday 23 October, but vulnerability matching is not done. Recruitment adverts are live, with a closing date of 26 October.

title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly Executive Team meeting: the damp deep-dive draft missed 23 October, Castlemere commits to clear heat pump faults by 6 November, four electrician applicants, the Ombudsman pack due Friday and Q2 commentary requests.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Silvering Homes Executive Team (Mondays 09:30-10:30, Teams). Action log kept by Tessa Morgan.

transcript.text: Morning all. Rachel, you're on mute... there we go.
Sorry. Morning!
Tessa, actions.

Martin, Castlemere programme - due today. Joanne, A06 in the tracker - due Friday. Gareth, deep-dive draft - due Friday. Gareth, Ombudsman job history - due tomorrow. Catherine, the Home First pre-read - due the twelfth.
Gareth. I didn't get a draft on Friday.

No. I'm sorry. Honestly, two things happened. Ellie was on leave, and when Kwame reconciled the breach numbers to FieldLoop - which internal audit told us to do - they didn't match what we'd reported in two months. So I didn't want to send you numbers I'd have to change.
I understand that, and I'd rather have right than quick. But the deadline to Hilary is Saturday.
I think I can still make the thirty-first. Just about.
Can I ask how big the difference is? Because the September board pack had a breach number in it.
A handful of cases. Some were coded as breaches when the resident refused access, which under the guidance... it's not straightforward. Kwame's going through each one.
If the board figure was wrong, we need to tell them, not just quietly change it.
Agreed. Gareth, the deep-dive needs to say clearly if any previously reported number has changed and why.
Yes. Will do.
Martin, Orchard Fields.

Better news, sort of. We finally got the programme on Friday. Castlemere say all eleven heat pump faults cleared by the sixth of November, and the rest of the defects by the end of November. The list is at a hundred and forty-three now.
It's going up?
Residents who've moved in are reporting new ones. Which is what the defects period is for, to be fair. Still eighteen unlet.
Can I make sure the new residents are getting a clear letter about how to report defects? We had two calls into the contact centre last week from people who didn't know.
I'll ask Chloe. Good point.
Simone, recruitment.
Closing date was Friday. Four applicants for the electrician posts, two for plasterer. Daniel's shortlisted three electricians. Interviews Wednesday the fourth at Aylesford.
If we get two, I'd like them to start before Christmas. The EICR backlog is still around thirty.
Rachel - Ombudsman.
Gareth, I'm still waiting for the job history. It's due Friday to the Ombudsman.
Kwame's doing it tomorrow. It'll be with you by Wednesday.
Wednesday latest, please. I need a day to check it.
Q2 paper, Joanne.
Martin's leading. The issue is commentary. Martin needs paragraphs from Rachel and Gareth.
By the sixth, please. I'll have the finance sections done by the tenth.
Fine.
Yep.
And Joanne, A06 - did that get updated?
Ah. Not yet. I'll do it this week, I promise.
Okay. That's us. Thanks everyone. Gareth, Saturday.

recap.summary: The damp deep-dive draft missed its 23 October date. When Kwame Asante reconciled the breach figures to FieldLoop, as internal audit recommended, they did not match the figures reported in two months, partly because no-access cases had been coded as breaches. The deep-dive must explain any change to figures already reported to the board. Gareth Price still aims to meet the Chair's 31 October deadline. Castlemere will clear the 11 heat pump faults by 6 November and the other defects by the end of November. Defects have risen to 143 and 18 homes are still unlet. Electrician interviews are on 4 November. The Ombudsman job history is promised by 28 October, for submission on 30 October. RSH action A06 has still not been updated in the tracker.

title: Executive Team weekly
summary: Weekly Executive Team meeting: the Chair's email about the missed damp deep-dive, which moves to the 26 November board with an interim note by 6 November; Ombudsman pack submitted; October repairs; heat pump fixes; electrician interviews; Q2 paper deadlines; and A06 still not updated.
description: Weekly operational meeting of the Silvering Homes Executive Team (Mondays 09:30-10:30, Teams). Action log kept by Tessa Morgan.
agenda: Q2 board paper and strategy day

transcript.text: Morning. I'm going to start with Hilary's email, because you've all seen it. Gareth, the deep-dive didn't go on Saturday.
No. And I didn't tell anyone it wouldn't. That's my fault, and I've said so to you.
I appreciate that. Where is it, honestly?

Kwame's reconciliation is about two-thirds done. The headline from FieldLoop is {{fact:damp_cases_awaab}} cases under Awaab's Law, {{fact:damp_breaches}} with at least one breach. Most are written summaries late, then late investigations. The vulnerability match against Keystone isn't finished.
And is that twenty-five comparable to what went to the board in September?
Roughly. Some months moved up, some down. The deep-dive will have a table showing the changes.

Right. Here's what I propose. The full deep-dive goes to the board on the twenty-sixth, properly reconciled. Gareth sends Hilary an interim note by Friday with the headline numbers. I'll reply to her today and apologise. Joanne, does that work for the papers?
If the deep-dive is in the pack, it needs to be with me by the twelfth, like everything else.
Could I have until the sixteenth? I'd rather it was right.
That's Hilary's call, not mine. I'll ask her.
Do. Okay. Tessa, the rest of the log.

Gareth, Ombudsman job history - done, the twenty-eighth. Rachel, Ombudsman pack - submitted Friday. Martin, defect letter to new residents - done. Joanne, A06 in the tracker - not done. Rachel and Gareth, Q2 commentary - due Friday.
Ombudsman pack went on Friday at four. Thanks to Kwame for that, he did a lot of it.
Good. Joanne?
I know. It still says Complete. I updated the other actions on Friday and just... missed it. I'll do it straight after this. Sorry.
It does matter, because Marcia will look at the tracker before the board.
Understood.
Repairs. October.

Routine in target was {{sql:SELECT routine_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-10'}} per cent in October, up from about fifty-one in September. Overall {{sql:SELECT pct_in_target FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-10'}}. Emergencies ninety-eight and a half. So a little better, but nowhere near ninety.
And interviews are Wednesday. Three electricians shortlisted, two plasterers.
If we get two good sparks, I think we can be at seventy-five by February.
And if we don't?
Then we need agency cover, which is expensive. I'd want Martin's view.
Bring me a costed option after Wednesday.
Orchard Fields?
Seven of the eleven heat pumps fixed. Castlemere still say all by Friday. Still {{fact:newbuild_awaiting_let}} homes unlet. Void loss so far is in the development report.
The defect letter went out and the calls have stopped, so thank you.
Q2 and the strategy day. Joanne.

Deadline's the twelfth. I've sent the reminder. Strategy day at Linton Lodge on the twenty-sixth, business meeting in the morning, strategy from half eleven. Lunch with SilverLiving residents, which Margaret's organising.
I'll do the Copilot interim update. Two weeks in - the complaints team say it's saving them about an hour per stage 1 response.
That's exactly the kind of evidence the board wants. Okay. I think that's it. Gareth, Hilary, Friday.
Friday. Understood.

recap.summary: The Chair emailed because the damp deep-dive (BA-26/31) missed its 31 October deadline. The full, reconciled deep-dive will now go to the 26 November board. Gareth Price will send the Chair an interim note by Friday 6 November, and Joanne Pike will ask the Chair whether the paper can arrive on 16 November. Headline figures: {{fact:damp_cases_awaab}} Awaab's Law cases, {{fact:damp_breaches}} with a breach. The Ombudsman evidence pack for CMP-24019 was submitted on 30 October. RSH action A06 still shows Complete in the tracker, three weeks after the committee reopened it. October routine repairs reached {{sql:SELECT routine_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month = '2026-10'}}% in target, with electrician interviews on 4 November. Seven of the 11 Orchard Fields heat pumps are fixed and {{fact:newbuild_awaiting_let}} homes remain unlet.
